newsitem.title: DUBAI: Mideast Gulf Oil Outlook - gas oil mired at lows.
newsitem.headline: Mideast Gulf Oil Outlook - gas oil mired at lows.

text.p: Gulf middle distillate markets are mired near two-year lows with scant prospects for any sustained recovery, Gulf-based traders said on Thursday.

Gulf gas oil has spiralled to its lowest level since August 1995 as demand from key Indian sub-continent and Far East markets evaporated, leaving unsold barrels in the hands of state refiners and traders.

Cargoes talked at $18.30 a barrel fob Gulf on Thursday, with premiums to published quotes heading for single digits after Indian Oil Corp's (IOC) decision last week to cancel its term middle distillate tender and pare back August spot requirements.

Only a decision by IOC to reissue its term tender coupled with higher sales to east Africa because of higher Mediterranean prices and anticipated maintenance work at Saudi Aramco's Ras Tanura refinery could turn the market around, traders said.
"I cannot see a real thread of hope in this market...The feeling is that the market remains depressed unless something drastic happens," said a trader based in the Gulf.
The key Singapore market, weighed down by rising inventories, was waiting fo renewed Chinese gas oil demand before recovering heavy losses.

One percent Gulf gas oil was talked at parity to 10 cents above the quote and 0.5 percent at plus 15-20 cents, faltering after IOC bought just 165,000 tonnes in its August tender, below market expectations of 400,000 tonnes.

A Kuwaiti kerosene cargo for second half July delivery was said sold at a five cents premium to independent price quotes, while Aramco was considering cancelling its tender for 32,000-35,000 tonnes of unleaded reformate because of low bids, traders said.
Seasonal demand weakness has also spilled over into liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) markets where discounts against Aramco's monthly contract price have continued to slip.
Saudi propane was said traded at a $10-15 discount to the official contract price of $175 a tonne, traders said.
Naphtha and fuel oil have shown more resilience, with naphtha maintaining a $10 premium to quotes and heavy fuel oil narrowing its discount to $2-3.
Fujairah 380 cst bunkers have followed a steady Singapore market, pushing slighly up to $97-99 a tonne.
